rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked all 9 chunks (0 lede + 8 `##` headers) under a sequential read; every pronoun/demonstrative resolves against same-chunk or earlier-chunk material (`Path 1/2/3` named in chunk 1 and reused in chunks 2,4,6; `gh` named chunk 2, reused chunk 5). Closest call: chunk 4 'Linear', line 77: 'Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path.' — 'the three trackers' resolves fully since GitHub (ch2), Jira (ch3) and Linear (this chunk) have all been named by this point; 'path' is lowercase generic English, not a dangling cite of the Path-1/2/3 system. Second-closest: chunk 7, line 108: '...Pairs with `managed-mcp.json` as the second half of tenant-side plugin policy' — 'second half' resolves within the same sentence (the just-described managed-settings.json mechanism is the first half); no forward or missing referent.

No phrase points at another curriculum file by position; every cross-reference is either an earlier-named term reused (rule 1's carve-out) or an external URL cited with descriptive link text. Closest call: chunk 1, line 15: 'Plugins distribute Path 2, `claude mcp add`, at scale, under *Plugins and marketplaces*.' — names the target section by its actual title, the sanctioned form under the navigational-pointer carve-out, not a positional pointer.

Every one of the 8 `##` chunks carries a self-standing claim beyond a wait-state. Thinnest chunk: 5 'Other trackers', lines 83-88 (5 body lines incl. Sources): 'Check the Anthropic Directory for reviewed connectors and your tracker's own docs. Most have a third-party MCP or a CLI fallback (like `gh`).' — short but a complete, standalone claim, not a context-dependent fragment.

Checked all 8 headers against their chunk content under the cover-the-body test. Most compound header: chunk 7, line 104: 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' — body delivers both clauses ('Official vs team marketplaces.' line 106; 'When plugins beat `claude mcp add`.' line 110). No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triple, no retracted-then-kept number, no abstraction-noun stack, no empty verb-triplet leg anywhere in the 8 chunks. Two candidates checked and cleared: chunk 2 line 23, 'no MCP server, no PAT management, no allowlist work for IT' is a 3-item list inside one sentence (not the banned 3-sentence pattern) and each leg is concrete and distinct (mechanism/credential/process), so it survives the 'new content per leg' test. Self-grading-superlative sub-item checked against chunk 4 line 77, 'Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers' — this grades a third-party product (Linear vs. GitHub/Jira MCP setups), not the training's own value; the harm this sub-item guards against (curriculum boasting about itself, per check_writing.md §13) is absent, so it doesn't trip this rule (flagged in notes for a research-claims/writing read, out of this class's lane).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'firing', 'compendium', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood', or 'Connections'-as-proper-noun anywhere; 'connector'/'action'/'tool' are Claude Code product vocabulary defined in-body (line 17), not authorial dialect. One judgment call: chunk 2 line 30, 'The surface is broad: every GitHub REST/GraphQL endpoint is reachable via `gh api`...' uses 'surface' as a noun, the banned shape's literal wording — but in context this is the ordinary SWE term 'API surface' (surface area of an API), universally parseable by an engineer in the room, distinct from this repo's own authorial sense of 'surface' (a generation/content region) that the rule's 'writing surface' example targets. Harm (dialect the room can't parse) is absent, so this stays a PASS rather than a REVISE.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lookup/reference surface, so the per-slide 1-bold budget is off, but the ≲5-word handle cap still binds. Chunk 1 'Three paths to a work-app action' is exactly the rule's named 'menu of options' shape (reader scans 3 paths to find their own), and for that shape the rule requires bolding the mode word alone ('**Path 2:**') with the title left plain — but line 12 bolds the FULL first clause: '**Path 2, `claude mcp add` from the command line.**' (9 words incl. a code span), and lines 11/13 do the milder version of the same thing ('**Path 1, connector inheritance.**' 4 words; '**Path 3, first-party CLI via Bash.**' ~6 words). Line 12 is the rule's own named failure shape verbatim: 'Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover.' Non-blocking per this class's partition (rule 9 = polish).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Bold only the mode word per item ('**Path 1:**', '**Path 2:**', '**Path 3:**') and leave the descriptive title in plain text, matching the Read:/Watch: exemplar in the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked git history for header changes: commit fa43db7c (2026-08-19, 'mcp plugins slide split') INSERTED '## Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' as a brand-new header directly above content ('Official vs team marketplaces.' / 'Enterprise pre-registration.' / 'When plugins beat...') that was written for and already matched this exact topic — a slide SPLIT, not a same-header-different-job RENAME (the rule's actual trigger: 'a commit that changes a `##` line without touching the bullets under it').
